item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in this repository (tasktracker package), following its acceptance criteria exactly. Operator's words: implement all tickets in BACKLOG.md, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add tests for what you build; standard library only; commit this ticket as its own commit.

TT-104: Undo.
`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Touch only what this ticket needs (tasktracker/store.py and tests). Do not change other tickets' areas.

model_reasons.implement: Stateful undo log with clear rules; balanced tier, standard review because it mutates store state.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in this repository (tasktracker package), following its acceptance criteria exactly. Operator's words: implement all tickets in BACKLOG.md, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add tests for what you build; standard library only; commit this ticket as its own commit.

TT-103: Search query syntax.
`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Touch only what this ticket needs (tasktracker/search.py and tests). Do not change other tickets' areas.

model_reasons.implement: Small tokenizer and matcher with clear spec; balanced tier suffices.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md in this repository (tasktracker package), following its acceptance criteria exactly. Operator's words: implement all tickets in BACKLOG.md, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add tests for what you build; standard library only; commit this ticket as its own commit.

TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export.
`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Touch only what this ticket needs (tasktracker/export.py and tests). Do not change other tickets' areas.

model_reasons.implement: Routine, well-specified serialization change; balanced tier suffices.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in this repository (tasktracker package), following its acceptance criteria exactly. Operator's words: implement all tickets in BACKLOG.md, following each ticket's acceptance criteria exactly; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add tests for what you build; standard library only; commit this ticket as its own commit.

TT-101: Reject impossible due dates.
`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Touch only what this ticket needs (tasktracker/dates.py and tests). Do not change other tickets' areas.

model_reasons.implement: Routine, well-specified parsing change; balanced tier suffices.

pr.body: Approach: tasktracker/dates.py adds InvalidDate(ValueError); ISO dates go through date() and ValueError is converted; offsets are limited to 1-9 digits (regex) and date overflow is converted. Files: tasktracker/dates.py, tests/test_dates.py (new). Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -> 12 tests OK (4 existing, 8 new). Review: the first reviewer found a huge-offset escape (ValueError), fixed in 50d5504 with a regex bound and a test; the second reviewer passed the delta; the third confirmed the finding resolved at the head. Assumptions: standard ISO YYYY-MM-DD only; offsets above 9 digits are treated as unsupported forms. Follow-up (non-blocking): InvalidDate messages echo the full input, which can be long for very long inputs.
pr.summary: parse_due no longer clamps impossible dates. now impossible dates, unsupported forms and bad offsets raise InvalidDate. before: 2026-02-30 -> 2026-02-28, now: InvalidDate with the original text.
pr.title: TT-101: reject impossible due dates

agt_01M8AQDXRHPW1F7FMK29Q5VZ69:1.description: The +Nd offset path calls int(offset.group(1)) outside any InvalidDate handling. An offset with more than 4300 digits (Python 3.14 int-string limit) raises a plain ValueError, which escapes parse_due as a non-InvalidDate exception. Reproduced: parse_due('+' + '9'*5000 + 'd', today) -> ValueError 'Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)'. Fix: bound the digits in OFFSET (e.g. \+(\d{1,9})d) or wrap the int(

risk.why: Behaviour change in tasktracker/dates.py: impossible ISO dates now raise instead of clamping, so callers relying on clamping would change. parse_due has no other callers in the repo. InvalidDate stays a ValueError, so existing handlers still catch it. Reviewers confirmed medium.
